newsitem.title: USA: Apple to cut 2,700 jobs in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Apple to cut 2,700 jobs in restructuring.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. said Friday it plans to cut 2,700 jobs in an effort to stop a slide in profits and revenues.
The troubled computer maker said the restructuring, the company's second major overhaul in the last 12 months, will result in $155 million charge in its second quarter ending in March.

"The top priorities guiding our reorganization are the rapid delivery of distinctive products for our loyal business, education, and home customers, and the development of a robust next-generation operating system to carry them into the future," Chairman Gilbert Amelio said in a statement.

"We can best achieve these goals by streamlining our organisation, simplifying our product lines to deliver fewer but much stronger models, and stopping investments in activities that are not central to these core businesses."

As part of the restructuring, Apple said it will reduce investment in some sections of its Mac Operating System software. These will include the Open Doc component software technology, Cyberdog, Open Transport, Game Sprockets, and Mac OS Development Tools.

Apple will halt funding for the Video Conferencing Solution and AIX Server Software and is exploring options for its Newton hand-held digital assistant. Apple said it will not produce Apple-branded Pippin devices, which enable television sets to access the Internet.

Apple said it is revising the delivery schedule for future Mac Operating System releases but it still plans to deliver Rhapsody in 1998. The company said it will also phase out its Performa Macintosh home computers this spring in favour of Power Mac models.
